 SC food pantry sees surge in families after SNAP cuts 
 Changes to the SNAP program have cut off many benefits for thousands of households statewide in South Carolina. By Juliana Alford Published : Oct. 23, 2026 at 7:17 PM EDT | Updated : 2 hours ago Share Add Us On Google Add as a preferred source on Google CONWAY, SC (WMBF) - Changes to the SNAP program have cut off many benefits for thousands of households statewide in South Carolina. 
 Families who rely on SNAP to stock their kitchens are turning to food pantries and other resources to keep meals on the table.
 Experts say that after President Trump’s “One Big Beautiful Bill” went into effect, roughly 13% of South Carolina households lost their SNAP benefits.
 Saundra Rhodes, director of Social Services in Georgetown, Horry, and Winnsboro counties, said the Salvation Army in Conway has seen more families come through its doors.
 “We’ve definitely seen an uptick in the number of families that are now coming to the pantry,” Rhodes said. “Just in the month of October alone, and we’re not even done with October, we’ve had 55 new families come through, and several of them had mentioned a reduction in their SNAP benefits.”
 That adds about 164 more people to feed in one month, according to Rhodes.
 “When I look at July, August, and September, we’ve doubled the number of people, the number of new families that are coming in,” Rhodes said.
 Rhodes said the reduction in benefits is her biggest concern.
 “The reductions are my biggest concern because people just don’t simply have the food they used to be able to get,” Rhodes said.
 With the holidays approaching, Rhodes said she is preparing to provide more food to meet demand.
 “We’ve had a lot more people asking, ‘What are we going to provide for Thanksgiving and for Christmas in order to help them?’ But we know that during the holidays we’re going to have to provide more, and so we prepare for it,” Rhodes said.
 Beginning next month , the South Carolina Department of Social Services will roll out “Healthy Food SC,” a two-year program to help SNAP recipients choose healthier options at the grocery store.
 Rhodes said The Salvation Army in Conway is accepting donations.
